text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs—open and merged—for two weeks. This lets us catch issues without blocking work, while gathering data on false positives and edge cases. The trade-off is temporary noise in PR comments, but it’s the fastest way to validate fixes across the full workflow.

name: Gauge
text: Running PR-Agent in shadow mode on all PRs poses a significant risk of training reviewers to dismiss all autofeedback as noise, not just the false positives. A better alternative might be to start with a small subset of PRs and gradually expand to minimize the impact on reviewers. This argument would be settled by data showing that reviewers can effectively distinguish between valid and false autofeedback after a trial period with a limited scope.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode only on merged PRs flagged as high-risk by a lightweight team rule (e.g., "changes >5 files"). This cuts noise by 80% while still catching edge cases in the riskiest work.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on merged PRs only for two weeks. This keeps the signal-to-noise ratio high for reviewers while still validating fixes across real work. The trade-off is missing data on open PRs, but that gap is small—most edge cases surface in merged PRs anyway.

name: Ratchet
text:
DECISION: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode *only on merged PRs* for two weeks to validate fixes without training reviewers to ignore feedback.

Result: Shadow mode data proves or disproves the fix’s value; owner Overhaul delivers a go/no-go report to the lead by end of pilot.
